memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and totally destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the people of Gibeon had made a treaty of peace with Israel and were living near them. He and his people were very much alarmed at this, because Gibeon was an important city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were good fighters. So Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem appealed to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon. "Come up and help me attack Gibeon," he said, "because it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites." — Josh 10:1-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what stirred these five kings to war: Gibeon had made peace with God's people. That was their crime in the eyes of Adoni-Zedek. Gibeon had thrown in its lot with Israel and Israel's God, and for that it now faced the fury of its former allies. Choosing God's side made Gibeon a target.

This is a pattern worth understanding. When someone turns to God, they often face opposition precisely because of that choice. The Gibeonites' decision to seek peace with Israel brought hostility from those who had once been their neighbours. Aligning with God can cost us relationships and provoke resistance we did not have before.

The name of Jerusalem's king is quietly ironic. "Adoni-Zedek" means "lord of righteousness," yet here he leads an alliance against God's people. A religious-sounding name is no guarantee of a right heart. Opposition to God sometimes wears respectable, even righteous-looking clothing.

Jesus told His followers plainly, "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first" (John 15:18). When we choose to follow Christ, we should not be surprised if it brings opposition. But we can take heart: the Gibeonites' choice to align with God's people, though it provoked enemies, was ultimately the choice that saved them. Standing with God may cost us, but it places us on the winning side, under His protection. The One we align ourselves with is more than able to defend His own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you experienced opposition simply because you chose to follow God?
2. Does a "righteous" name or reputation always mean a right heart?
3. How does it steady you to know that aligning with God places you under His protection?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when following You brings opposition, help me not to be surprised or shaken. Keep me faithful, knowing that standing with You places me safely on Your side. Amen.
